Subject: Terascope: Pricing & Commit for Redwood MAP

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the MAP approach. Procurement asked me to put our ask in writing so we can move toward an internal approval on our end. High level:

- Proposed commitment: $150,000 ARR (12-month) starting Jan 2028
- Requested commercial: 20% platform discount + $20k implementation credit (to offset onboarding hours)
- We need final terms and SOW by Oct 18 to hit our procurement window.

Attached is our updated MAP and evaluation milestones (Terascope_MAP_v3.pdf). Procurement flagged SOC 2 evidence and traceability for data residency — happy to coordinate with your security team.

Can you confirm whether that level of discount/credit is achievable and who on Redwood we should expect to sign-off? If needed, we can do a short call this week to align internal approvers.

Thanks,
Kelly

Hi Kelly — thanks for the clear ask and the MAP doc. Looping in Marissa (Finance) and Neha (Pricing) to scope approvals and credits.

Short answers: we can consider commit-based credits, but discount depths are tied to commit size and term. Two quick options we commonly use:

1) 12-month, $150k commit — commercial discount in the mid-teens (12–18%) + implementation credit up to $15k with standard SOW
2) 24-month, $150k ARR-equivalent (prepaid) — deeper discount (18–25%) and larger onboarding credit

To move this forward:
- Marissa/Neha: can you confirm whether 20% + $20k credit is within scope for VP approval or whether we need an exec exception?
- Kelly: are you able to flex on term (24 mo opt-in) or prepay structure? That would materially change the discount envelope.

I attached a draft SOW for our usual onboarding scope. If it helps, I'm happy to run a 30-minute MAP checkpoint this Friday to align on approvals and finalize a path to signature by Oct 18.

Best,
Rishi

On Oct 2, 2027, Rishi Malhotra wrote:
> I attached a draft SOW for our usual onboarding scope.

Thanks for the context — quick finance read before we present to VP:

- For a $150k ARR 12-month commitment we can typically approve up to an 18% platform discount at the AE/product team level, with an implementation credit capped at $15k. Anything beyond that (20%+ or credits > $15k) needs VP of Revenue approval.
- If Terascope moves to a 24-month prepay, we can be more aggressive (up to ~22% and larger credits) but we need legal to sign a prepaid addendum.
- We need the exact renewal/ESC clause language in the SOW (see SOW-draft.docx) — procurement will push on price protection and termination windows.

Actionable for Finance: please prepare a short approval memo if Rishi wants to request >18% or >$15k credit.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Rishi/Marissa — adding pricing detail.

Quoted:
> Two quick options we commonly use:

We should present a clean MAP-friendly offer set to Terascope. My recommendation:

A — Standard MAP: 12 months, $150k ARR
  - Discount: 15% (AE approval)
  - Implementation credit: $10k (no exec approval)
  - Payment: Net 30 monthly invoices

B — Accelerated MAP (preferred): 24 months prepay (equivalent $300k)
  - Discount: 20% (requires VP approval)
  - Implementation credit: $20k (requires VP approval)
  - Benefit: price protection for term, faster onboarding scheduling

If Kelly insists on 20% + $20k for a 12-month term we will need an exec credit/discount exception that must include:
- Deal memo with ARR math and expected 12-month gross margin impact
- Approval from VP Revenue and Head of Finance

I attached a quick pricing model (pricing_model_v2.csv) showing margin impact for each option.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
